thread:
support_jess: FYI - multiple Dedicated customers in northeast region are getting 429s + placement failures since ~08:10 UTC. Customers reporting long tail latency too. Raising to incidents.

oncall_maya: I'm looking. Do we have a single point or widespread? Any errors in placement service?

support_jess: Customers see `rpc: placement denied` and `GPU allocation timeout`. Example customer trace: `req_id=9f2a alloc_err=placement_failed region=us-northeast zone=a`

eng_liam: Can you paste a minimal repro request? Model + config? Also any recent scaling events?

cust_ops_tom: Customer A (acct 8921) repro: POST /v1/dedicated/infer model=gpt-small-dq qps=80 batch=1, gets 429s after initial successes. They reported autoscale did not add nodes.

autoscale-bot: [ALERT] 08:13 UTC autoscaling: policy "dedicated-default" attempted scale-up but quota check failed -> no new instance created.

infra_alan: Quota check failed? Which quota? I only see compute reserved pools near capacity in us-northeast. Investigating host provisioning errors.

eng_liam: Stack traces show placement service timed out waiting for allocation candidates; there are many preemptible reclaim events on a subset of hosts (noisy-tenant eviction flood) causing allocations to fail fast.

support_jess: Customers also reported unexpected 401s intermittently around the same time — might be collateral from retries hitting fallback endpoints?

billing_olga: Billing events show spikes in token billing retries for affected accounts, but no billing blocks. Not seeing invoice-related auth revocations.

oncall_maya: Immediate mitigation: 1) divert placement attempts to us-west-2 via routing policy for impacted projects, 2) disable aggressive reclaim on candidate hosts, 3) manually kick an emergency scale-up. Can infra confirm capacity to cold-start?

infra_alan: Cold-start queued. Provisioning stuck on a rate limit from cloud provider (API 429 provisioning). Opening cloud ticket. Meanwhile we can failover traffic to west within routing rules.

eng_liam: Added canary route rule to send 30% traffic to us-west-2, leaving 70% local to avoid cold start blast. Patch pushed to routing service. `deploy-bot: deploy routing v2.14 -> success`

deploy-bot: routing-service v2.14 deployed by eng_liam at 08:28 UTC.

autoscale-bot: [UPDATE] 08:30 UTC autoscaling: manual override succeeded, provisioning 2 reserved instances. Estimated ready in ~7m.

support_jess: Customer A confirms reduced 429s but still seeing latency spikes for long queries.

eng_liam: Those latency spikes correlate with KV-cache misses from cross-region fallback. When routing flips, seq-latency increases for cold sessions. We should set TTL for KV prefixes to 30m for failing projects to avoid thrash.

infra_alan: Applied temporary rule to increase prefix cache TTL for impacted accounts. Also removed the noisy tenant from candidate pool (isolated) — its workloads had extreme eviction churn.

cust_ops_tom: Customer B had a critical job and saw a failed canary at 08:34; ops asked for immediate rollback of one route. Can we route that customer's requests back to local after the manual instances are healthy?

oncall_maya: Yes — plan: keep canary in place, monitor allocation success rate for 15m. If error rate < 1% then move customer's traffic back.

eng_liam: Post-mortem notes so far:
- Root cause: regional GPU stockout combined with noisy-tenant-induced reclaim churn prevented autoscale from stabilizing (cloud quota/provision rate limits amplified issue).
- Secondary: routing fallback caused KV cache cold starts and transient 401s on auth proxy under retries.
- Mitigations applied: emergency provisioning, manual routing canary, increase KV TTL, quarantine noisy tenant, cloud rate-limit escalation ticket.

billing_olga: We should flag impacted accounts for credit review. I'll start a billing review ticket.

support_jess: Customers notified of mitigation steps. One customer asked for timeline to complete capacity restoration. ETA from infra?

infra_alan: New instances should be ready by 08:38 UTC. Cloud support confirmed rate-limit window clears at ~08:40. I'll update when nodes are `ready` in fleet.

autoscale-bot: [UPDATE] 08:39 UTC - 2 reserved instances active in us-northeast. Allocation acceptance increased.

cust_ops_tom: Customer A reports normal behavior restored at 08:42. Slow queries still have a small tail but acceptable.

eng_liam: We'll follow up with a runbook change: - detect reclaim churn -> automatically quarantine hosts; - add backoff before aggressive cross-region failover to prevent KV cold thrash; - add preflight quota check and retry strategy for autoscale.

oncall_maya: Logging this as SEV3 (regional capacity). I'll start the incident ticket and add owners for runbook and postmortem.

support_jess: Thanks team. I'll consolidate customer emails and post incident summary to #incidents after the postmortem draft. :thumbsup:

eng_liam: For the postmortem include these logs snippets: ```
placement.err=placement_failed candidates=0 reclaim_count=42 host_id=host-7a
autoscale.err=quota_check_failed reason=provider_rate_limit
auth.proxy=401 retry=3 path=/v1/dedicated/auth
```

noncall_maya: Closing loop: any follow-ups? If not, I'll hand to eng-runbook to action.

support_jess: No further asks from customers right now. Marking as monitoring.

eng_liam: I'll own runbook changes. Adding tasks to backlog.

billing_olga: I'll propose customer credits for affected time window.

support_jess: Thread will be summarized in incident ticket 2412-NE-capacity.

deploy-bot: incident-ticket created: 2412-NE-capacity by oncall_maya.

support_jess: Thanks all. Closing active escalation; we'll monitor for 24h. :white_check_mark:
